seed: The five the app comes with, on the shelf of a document that has taken none of them: Button, Text Field, Card, Nav Bar and Badge, with nothing typed in the search box. This is the walk that OWNS them. On 2026-09-17 a walk written about where words sit in a box was the only thing that noticed the Nav Bar tile could not be reached, and the audit that hit it concluded the app had lost the component; a starter going missing has to break the walk written for starters instead. Then it builds the way a person builds: three off the shelf in a row, checking after each one that the panel is looking at the thing that just landed. Until 2026-09-23 it checked the opposite — that the SHELF was still on screen — and that is what the dock was doing at the cost of the new component's own section, which ended up above the top of the panel (filed 2026-09-22). The shelf now comes back only as far as the new component's section can afford, so on the Button, which is short, it comes back whole, and on the Nav Bar, which is not, it stops a few points under the edge.

steps.note: THE TEST: all five tiles are on the Components shelf of a fresh document, with nothing typed. Every one of them is built and answers to its name, which is what a person means by finding one.

THE TEST: the Nav Bar came off the shelf and is in the picture as the original, AND the panel is looking at it: the Component section naming what just landed is whole, at the top, with no scrolling. Placing it opened Component, Appearance, Effects, Motion and Layout above the shelf, and the dock brings the shelf back after you only as far as that section can afford.

WHAT THIS SHOWS: a SECOND starter fetched after the first one was placed, with no scrolling of the panel in between. The Card is under the shelf's own fold, so the shelf scrolls to it the way a person scrolls to it.

steps.comment: The Button's sections are short enough that the shelf can come all the way back under them, so this is the drop where both ends of the rule are visible at once: the thing you placed at the top, the shelf you placed it from at the foot.

steps.note: THE TEST: three starters off the shelf one after another, and after every one of them the panel is looking at what landed rather than at the shelf. This is what building a screen out of components actually is.
